conviction_note: Findings sum to +0.9: peers that reported after Sweetgreen last spoke (CMG 10-Q on 2026-10-28, CAVA on 2026-11-04) show the cyclospora demand hit faded within Q3, and the FY SSS guide of -8% to -7% leaves room against very easy Q4 compares. That is offset by a stock already +133% off its low, trading above the average target, with call-heavy open interest and a history of 5 of 7 prints down. p_up is 53 on a 12% absolute move, so the scaled number (+0.72) is close to the sum. The recovery thesis is a proxy, and much of it was published by Wells Fargo and KeyBanc in Sep/Oct.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$170M (Earnings Whispers $169.6M and OpenCapital $170.1M agree; Yahoo $168.8M from 11 analysts; Chartmill $173.6M and FXEmpire $174.0M sit higher, so the bar is roughly agreed within ~3%). EPS ~-$0.25 to -$0.28. The company guide is FY26 SSS -8% to -7%, RLM 10.5-11.0%, adj. EBITDA $(27)-(23)M, ~13 net new units (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001477815/000162828026054324/q226sweetgreenearningsrele.htm). With H1 SSS at -12.8% and -6.2%, the guide implies H2 averaging about -4.5% to -6.5%. With H1 adj. EBITDA at -$8.3M, it implies H2 of about -$15M to -$19M. H1 non-comp contribution was ~10 points (Q1 revenue -2.9% on SSS -12.8%; Q2 +3.8% on -6.2%), so a ~$170M revenue consensus against $172.4M in Q3'25 implies a Street Q3 SSS around -8% to -10%. That is my derivation; no sourced Q3 SSS consensus was found. Sources: https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/SG, https://www.opencapital.sh/stocks/sg, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SG/analysis/
positioning_check: Short interest 24.10M shares on the 2026-10-15 settlement (~20.2% of 119M shares outstanding; the sweep's Fintel figure was 23.2% of float), 5.29 days to cover, down from 25.37M on 09-15; Equibles estimates ~23.0M for 10-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/sg/shortinterest). The 25-delta skew is -3.97 vol points, so upside is paid; put/call OI is 0.10 and the straddle implies 13.5%. Hedge funds hold large stakes: Millennium 5.4% (13G/A, event 2026-09-29, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1477815/000110465926114138/primary_doc.xml) and Baillie Gifford 8.0% (13G/A, event 2026-09-30, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1477815/000108887526000067/primary_doc.xml). The setup is crowded on both sides: a heavy short base plus call-heavy longs who have ridden a 130% rally.

findings.finding: Two fast-casual peers that reported after Sweetgreen's 2026-08-06 guide cut say the food-safety demand hit faded within Q3. Chipotle's Q3 10-Q (filed 2026-10-28): headwinds began in July, worsened for several weeks, and comps were back to pre-headwind levels by end of August. CAVA's Q3 release (2026-11-04): cyclospora cut Q3 SRS by only ~150bp, Q3 SRS was +3.1%, and FY SRS was RAISED to 6.0-7.0% from 4.5-6.5%. Sweetgreen's own FY SSS guide of -8% to -7% was cut from -4% to -2% on an 'uncertain' recovery, and management put the July hit at ~600bp, so a category recovery by Sept/Oct supports a held-to-raised SSS guide on Thursday.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide cut on the outbreak (2026-08-06) drew -8.0%. Q1 2026, where management cited April improving to ~-8%, drew +1.9%. 5 of 7 prior prints fell, and SG has not been paid much for good sales news.
findings.why_not_priced: The CAVA release came out last night, so SG had only today's session to react, and SG's 5-day return is -4.2%, not up. The sell-side recovery calls (Wells Fargo 2026-09-28, KeyBanc 2026-10-23) were channel checks, not a peer's audited Q3 comp with a quantified cyclospora drag. If this were fully priced, SG would trade near the $11-12 bull targets, not -7% from its 52-week high, and the 13.5% straddle would not be wider than SG's 8% median move. Partly priced: the stock is +133% off its low.
findings.independence: Two documents from two companies: CAVA's 8-K (above) and Chipotle's 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001058090/000105809026000104/cmg-20260930.htm). Wells Fargo's checks pointed the same way ('recovery taking hold in September'; traffic and comps essentially back to the pre-outbreak pattern by end of Q3; https://www.briefs.co/?p=22951). All three are proxies, not a Sweetgreen number.

findings.finding: The FY26 SSS guide of -8% to -7% is soft arithmetic against the compares. H1 SSS was -12.8% and -6.2%, so the guide implies an H2 average of about -4.5% to -6.5%, against prior-year compares of -9.5% (Q3'25) and -11.5% (Q4'25). The pre-outbreak guide (-4% to -2%) implied H2 around +3.5%. If the company-quantified ~600bp July drag faded by September, as peers report, then Q3 near -7% and Q4 near -4% land at the guide midpoint, and a flat-to-positive Q4 puts the top end or a raise in play.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what SG trades on: -8.0% on the 2026-08-06 cut, -9.6% on 2026-02-26 and -23.1% on 2025-08-07, both of which carried guide reductions.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Q3 revenue (~$170M) still implies a Street Q3 SSS around -8% to -10%, so estimates have not been rebuilt for a fast recovery, and the average price target ($8.63) sits below spot. If the market had fully priced a raise, the average target would not lag the price by 20%. Partly priced through the rally and the Wells Fargo/KeyBanc upgrades.
findings.independence: Shares the recovery thesis with the CAVA/CMG finding but rests on a different document (Sweetgreen's own guide and compares). Q1 2026 compare and April -8% from https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260507512857/en/Sweetgreen-Inc.-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results. July ~600bp drag from https://www.nrn.com/fast-casual/sweetgreen-downgrades-guidance-despite-improving-trends. The two findings are not independent evidence of recovery; they are sized separately because one is a peer datum and the other is the company's own bar arithmetic.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue consensus (~$169.6-170.1M at Earnings Whispers and OpenCapital, $168.8M at Yahoo) is about -1.5% to -2% YoY against $172.4M in Q3'25. With the ~10-point non-comp contribution seen in Q1 and Q2 2026, that implies a Q3 SSS bar around -8% to -10%. A Q3 at about -7% (underlying ~-3% with an easier compare, plus a 600bp July drag fading through September) would be a ~1-2% revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SG missed revenue in each of the last four quarters. Q2 2026: $192.7M against $194.5-200.7M estimates, -8.0% (driven by the guide). Q1 2026 missed EPS and rose +1.9% on improving monthly comps.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimate sources disagree by ~$5M ($168.8M-$174.0M), which suggests stale estimates were not all rebuilt after the September recovery checks. If consensus had moved up with the stock, the low end would not sit at -2% YoY. Inference from a derived SSS bar, so sized small.
findings.independence: Revenue cross-check at https://www.opencapital.sh/stocks/sg ($170.1M) and https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SG/analysis/ ($168.8M, 11 analysts). The SSS translation is my own arithmetic from the Q1 and Q2 releases, which share the guide finding's documents.

findings.finding: Positioning leans against more upside on the print. Spot $10.94 is +133% off the 52-week low and +14% over 20 sessions, about 27% above the MarketBeat average target of $8.63 (consensus Hold: 6 Buy, 9 Hold, 3 Sell; MarketBeat 2026-10-28). Option open interest is call-dominated (put/call 0.10) with upside paid in the skew. The recovery thesis is already in published upgrades (Wells Fargo to Overweight 2026-09-28, KeyBanc target $12 on 2026-10-23). Against that, ~24.1M shares (~20% of shares outstanding) are short at 5.3 days to cover, which is squeeze fuel on a clean guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of 7 prior prints fell, with a median absolute move of 8.0%. The two up prints were +1.9% and +0.04%, and no print in the window rose more than 2%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the market's own price and positioning. The finding is that the bar for a positive reaction has risen with the rally. If it were not a risk, the stock would trade below the average target and put OI would not be a tenth of call OI. The negative is shrunk for the crowded short (20% of shares out, 5.3 DTC; https://equibles.com/stocks/sg/shortinterest).
findings.independence: Run-up and skew come from the sealed baseline; short interest from FINRA via Equibles. Wells Fargo upgrade details at https://www.briefs.co/?p=22951.

findings.finding: Sweetgreen has missed the revenue consensus in each of the last four reported quarters. Q2 2026 revenue was $192.7M against $194.5M (MarketBeat) and $200.7M (other) estimates, and Q1 2026 was $161.5M, -2.9% YoY. A fifth sales miss is the base rate unless the outbreak recovery was sharp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The misses have coincided with down moves on 5 of 7 prints: -8.0%, -9.6%, -7.5%, -23.1%, -16.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus keeps being set above delivery. If the market fully discounted the pattern, the stock would not trade above the average target into the print. Small, because the pattern is public.
findings.independence: Q2 miss confirmed at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-sweetgreen-nyse-sg-shares-up-77-time-to-buy-2026-10-28/. This cuts against the revenue-beat inference above, and the two are left at small opposite sizes because the bar is a derived number.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-27 the board adopted an executive Severance Plan with an explicit change-in-control tier: the CEO and Chief Concept Officer get 1.5x salary, full acceleration of time-vesting equity and 18 months of COBRA on a termination within 12 months of a change in control (8-K filed 2026-08-31). This is strategic optionality that a Q3 call could address. Nothing in the filing says a process exists.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior strategic-review disclosure on an SG print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a quiet item 5.02 8-K with no wire coverage found. If the market read it as an M&A signal, a takeover premium narrative would appear in the analyst notes, and none does. Most likely routine, hence the tiny size.

baseline_tension: The peer and guide-arithmetic findings agree with the upside-paid skew (-4.0) and the +14% 20-day run-up, which is exactly why they are probably mostly priced. The one thing cutting against them is the name's own history of selling off on 5 of 7 prints and spot sitting above the average target.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the derived Q3 SSS bar rests on estimates that disagree by ~$5M and on my own non-comp arithmetic, so the reported-quarter beat finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.3.

Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): the positioning negative was cut from -1.2 to -0.6, and the separate +0.3 short-covering/squeeze finding was merged into it (Lesson 3: one finding with one sign per concern).
'What has worked' (a peer's print landing after the company last spoke): kept the CAVA/CMG guidance finding at +1.0 and did not shrink it further; p_up moved from 52 to 53.
Lesson 1 (reaction history veto): already reflected in the small reported-quarter sizes, and left standing.
